correctness.rationale: The old modules are exactly run intervals or quotient intervals containing the entire cyclic block. Every prime added-point type is characterized by alternating run bits, source/sink boundary bits and two explicit exceptional constraints. The exhaustive module-by-subset C++ checker verified every new-point orientation for all n from 4 through 12, totalling 458720 cases, with an independently written Python enumeration of all reversed arcs through n=8. These finite tests corroborate the modular proof and do not replace its all-size argument. The n=4 boundary and disjoint exceptional cases are explicit.

value.rationale: The classical prime one-point extension question is naturally about how many complete types witness primality, not solely whether one exists. The uniform finite multiplicities 0,1,6,8 and polynomial global count give an exact quantitative refinement across all parameter lengths and all single-arc perturbation positions, with a sharp upper bound independent of n. The 0/1 versus 6/8 jump identifies the structural effect of a nonadjacent reversal. This is a motivated structural classification, not a numerical lookup at a chosen small size.
